briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 25, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis Warning: Nepal Floods and Compound Disasters
sections.content: Regarding the recent major floods in Nepal, the Nepalese Prime Minister characterized them as 'a warning from climate change to the world' and urged international support [1, 16, 19, 21, 30, 31, 32, 34, 35, 37]. The Nepalese leader stated that his country is paying the price for climate change, raising his voice to admonish leaders on climate change at the UN [19, 24]. This sentiment reflects the international recognition that climate change is a fundamental cause exacerbating disasters [20], once again emphasizing the need for a global emergency response.

sections.title: ⚠️ The Deepening Reality of Climate Change and Its Widespread Impacts
sections.content: The impacts of climate change are being observed widely across the globe. A study has revealed that three glaciers in British Columbia (BC), Canada, face extinction within decades [36], and Antarctic sea ice continues to show 'alarming' low extents, recording its third smallest winter maximum extent since satellite records began [44]. Climate change is directly affecting human daily life and ecosystems as a whole, impacting the migration of birds of prey [25] and disrupting summer travel [15]. Domestically, the appearance of sharks in the artificial waterway of Busan's North Port, drawing an unusually large crowd, has been linked to the severity of the climate crisis [14].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Renewable Energy and Carbon Neutrality Efforts
sections.content: Positive progress in response to climate change has also been reported. In Australia's main electricity market, the share of renewable energy reached a record high of 80.5% [9]. Domestically, ESR acquired Aquila Clean Energy APAC, securing 1.6 GW of renewable energy in the region, including Korea [11], and GS is also expanding its power generation affiliates, focusing on wind power [12]. At the local government level, Yongin City is offering benefits of up to 100,000 KRW to participants in the carbon neutrality points program for the automotive sector [5, 6, 7], and Okcheon County is also recruiting new participants for the carbon neutrality points program year-round, encouraging citizens' voluntary participation in carbon reduction [8]. Furthermore, the UK is expanding its international contributions by providing 330 million pounds to the Global Environment Facility for climate change response [38].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Climate Adaptation, Policy Discussions, and Challenges
sections.content: Domestic and international policy and technological cooperation for climate change adaptation and mitigation are also actively underway. The Korea Rural Community Corporation expanded its technical cooperation on agricultural production infrastructure with Taiwan, discussing important agendas such as climate change and AI-driven water management [2]. Domestically, 'grid contribution' assessments are being conducted for solar and wind power generation facilities in the Jeju region, which will affect settlement amounts, indicating ongoing policy efforts for the stable integration of renewable energy into the power grid [13]. However, the importance of financial support for sustainable agriculture has also been highlighted. In England, funds for the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) were depleted within six hours of applications opening, leaving farmers who experienced crop failures due to the climate crisis without crucial financial support, demonstrating the urgent need for continuous funding for such policies [43].

briefing.closing: This concludes today's climate briefing for September 25, 2026. Thank you.
